what: a gate script substituted through PROPOSAL_GATE_PATH or QUALITY_GATE_PATH could report AUDIT-VALID or SUBMISSION-READY
escaped: the loader checked that the replacement exposed the expected functions, not that it was the packaged gate
mechanism: unified_gate.py keeps GATE_OVERRIDES and unverified_gate_overrides(): a differing override is warned about, refused for mode=submission and never yields AUDIT-VALID or SUBMISSION-READY, while a byte-identical copy stays allowed (test_audit_remediation.GateOverrideTests)

what: gate_mutation_probe could count something other than a failing test as a killed mutation
escaped: the classifier accepted failure evidence other than unittest's own failure headers
mechanism: classify() counts only unittest FAIL headers and treats a green exit that still prints one as an error, so a mutation is killed only by a test that failed (test_audit_remediation)

what: release archives and installs could include untracked local files under skills/
escaped: file selection walked the working tree instead of the tracked files
mechanism: install_skill.release_files and package_plugin use tracked files only and refuse when local files sit under skills/ (test_audit_remediation)

what: hook_guard_bash.py missed destructive commands hidden by shell syntax: &, subshells, if and for bodies, substitutions and abbreviated git options
escaped: the guard matched words in the command text without parsing quoting or control operators
mechanism: shlex tokenizing with control operators, substitutions() and abbreviates(); unparsable or deeply nested input fails closed (test_audit_hook_and_manifest.HookParsingTests)

what: an install kept files that the new release no longer ships
escaped: installs copied files in and never recorded which ones they owned
mechanism: .install-manifest.json records every installed file; a later install prunes only unedited files it owns and reports edited ones (test_audit_hook_and_manifest.InstallManifestTests)

what: two concurrent deck_check renders could fail because they shared one LibreOffice profile
escaped: render() used the default user profile, which one running conversion locks
mechanism: every render passes -env:UserInstallation with a throwaway profile (test_audit_maintenance.RenderIsolationTests)

what: the hook guard passed destructive commands that hid the target in a variable assigned in the same command, piped text into a shell, or used a Windows path
escaped: words were judged as written, variables were never expanded, and backslashes in Windows paths were consumed as shell escapes
mechanism: same-command variables are expanded before judging, text and base64 piped into a shell are denied, and Windows paths are normalised before tokenizing; the docstring lists what stays outside the guard's view (test_audit_residual_risks)

what: test_emit_render_without_soffice_is_not_verified failed on a host whose Python interpreter ships next to LibreOffice
escaped: the test emptied PATH to hide soffice, which also hid the interpreter's own libraries and did not hide a soffice installed beside the interpreter
mechanism: the test patches shutil.which in the running process instead of editing PATH (test_deck_pipeline)

what: the entry SKILL.md did not say that missing bidder material means intake-incomplete, and its wording read as if missing evidence meant conditional-bid; a Codex run that opened only that file recommended a conditional bid with no owner or deadline
escaped: the rule was written in the playbook and the evidence reference, and no test checked that the file every host opens first carries it
mechanism: Phase A of the entry SKILL.md states the intake-incomplete and conditional-bid conditions (test_skill_schema.py::EntrySkillBidDecisionTests)
